analysis: Examined the EngineV2Bridge.swift head excerpt (lines 508-639) and the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift patch and base text. Changes: (1) The EngineV2Bridge change is a comment-only edit at lines 124-125 (the stopStringScope doc comment). The visible head excerpt is constructor tail code for prefix-cache status and evidence wiring, which is not in the changed ranges. (2) In MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine the media path computes reasoningPrefix before bridge.submitTokenized, rather than after. It passes a new per-request stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope(reasoningParser:reasoningPrefix:)) to submitTokenized. The same scope is added to the text path at about line 1043 and to the cluster path at about line 1426 (reasoningPrefix nil). The two post-submit checkFirstContentDeadline calls around the prefix computation are removed. Security view: the reordering only moves a pure computation (tokenizer decode of the prompt tail) ahead of submission. That introduces no new trust boundary crossing. The removed deadline checks are still covered by the check after submit, and the failure path calls bridge.cancel and releaseBox.fire, so reservations should still be released. The stop-string scope only affects where client stop strings match, i.e. output truncation. It is not a confidentiality or authorization control, and I see no new exposure of A-001 (prompts) or the prefix-cache surface in T-041. The stop scope is not part of the cache salt or lookup tags, and the SSD cache identity and AAD are unchanged. Open questions for integration: the ReasoningStopScope implementation and the bridge's handling of a per-request stopStringScope were not visible, and neither was the final patch excerpt (truncated). I could not verify that a per-request scope cannot cause the stop-string filter to be bypassed or leak reasoning content into the content channel (T-056-style overclaim, low risk). No findings.
